summary: The change implements RegExp.prototype[Symbol.match] in its own file, following the spec steps in order. Step 2 throws a TypeError for a non-object this. Step 3 converts the argument with ToString before Get(regexp, "flags"). Steps 5 to 10 follow the spec, including the empty-match lastIndex advance via ToLength, AdvanceStringIndex and Set(..., true). Every abstract operation propagates errors with `?`. Nothing is special-cased, hardcoded or defaulted. The only remaining failures in the gate report come from the RegExp.prototype.flags getter, which lives in another file and throws the honest not-implemented error. Minor differences from the spec's `!` assertions (ArrayCreate(0) and CreateDataPropertyOrThrow use `?`) cannot fail on these inputs, so they have no observable effect. The `_new_target` rename and the removed non-step NOTE/name comments are harmless. I could not read the imported helpers (support::regexp::regexp_exec and advance_string_index) because they are outside the diff, so I did not verify their internals.
notes_for_next_attempt: No defects found in this diff. Once RegExp.prototype.flags is implemented in its own file, the remaining Symbol.match tests should be re-run to confirm they pass. The imported helpers in support::regexp (regexp_exec, advance_string_index) were not visible in this review and should be checked separately if they are not already covered by other tickets.
